title: Annealing-enhanced spin-orbit effects in non-centrosymmetric superconducting NbRe films
authors: Zahra Makhdoumi Kakhaki, Yuriy Yerin, Francesco Avitabile, Abhishek Kumar, Francesco Colangelo, Carla Cirillo, Oleksandr V. Dobrovolskiy, Carmine Attanasio
abstract: $\text{Nb}_{0.18}\text{Re}_{0.82}$ (NbRe) is a non-centrosymmetric superconductor with a transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ reaching $9\text{ K}$ in bulk form. While bulk and single-crystalline NbRe exhibit signatures of multigap superconductivity, thin films generally display a single-gap superconducting state due to structural disorder and reduced crystallite dimensions. Here, we investigate the impact of thermal annealing on the superconducting and normal-state magnetotransport properties of NbRe films. The temperature dependence of the upper critical field, $B_{\mathrm{c2}}(T)$, is analyzed within the microscopic Werthamer--Helfand--Hohenberg (WHH) framework, while the normal-state magnetoconductivity is described using the three-dimensional Kawabata weak-localization/weak-anti-localization model. Annealing drives a pronounced change in the electronic response, manifested by a strong weak anti-localization behavior in the normal state and an upper critical field that surpasses both the conventional orbital-limiting field and the Pauli paramagnetic limit. The microscopic analysis reveals a strong intrinsic increase in the relative spin--orbit scattering strength, with the annealed film showing a significantly enhanced spin--orbit-to-dephasing field ratio. These findings provide direct, independent evidence that thermal modification of the NbRe microstructure successfully amplifies spin--orbit-mediated quantum transport, which acts as the key mechanism protecting the non-centrosymmetric superconducting state against paramagnetic pair-breaking well beyond conventional theoretical boundaries.
summary: This work investigates how thermal annealing modifies the superconducting properties of non-centrosymmetric NbRe films. By analyzing both magnetotransport and critical field data, the authors demonstrate that annealing significantly amplifies spin-orbit coupling effects. This enhancement provides evidence for a mechanism protecting the unconventional superconductivity beyond standard theoretical bounds.
main_problem: The study investigates how thermal annealing affects superconducting and normal-state magnetotransport properties in non-centrosymmetric NbRe films, specifically focusing on the enhancement of spin-orbit effects.
main_result: Annealing significantly enhances spin-orbit-mediated quantum transport by increasing the relative spin-orbit scattering strength, leading to upper critical fields that exceed conventional theoretical limits and confirming strong antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling.
method: The research combines structural characterization (XRD) with detailed magnetotransport measurements, analyzing data using the Werthamer–Helfand–Hohenberg framework for $B_{c2}(T)$ and the 3D Kawabata weak-localization/weak-anti-localization model.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Nb}_{0.18}	ext{Re}_{0.82}$ thin films, which are non-centrosymmetric superconductors. The analysis relies on models describing quantum interference effects (WL/WAL) and superconducting pair-breaking mechanisms (WHH).
key_observables: Upper critical field $B_{c2}(T)$, normal-state magnetoconductivity ($\Delta\sigma/\sigma_0$), spin-orbit scattering strength ($B_{so}$), and the ratio $B_{so}/B_\phi$.
important_parameters: Annealing temperature, crystallite size increase (from $\sim 2$ nm to $\sim 10$ nm), and the observation that $B_{c2}(T)$ surpasses both orbital-limiting and Pauli paramagnetic limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that magnetotransport deviations from conventional theory are due to enhanced spin-orbit coupling protecting the superconducting state against Zeeman splitting.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD patterns confirming crystallite growth upon annealing, $R(T)$ curves showing $	ext{T}_c$ changes, and magnetoconductivity plots demonstrating pronounced Weak Anti-Localization (WAL) behavior in annealed samples compared to as-grown ones.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first characterizing structural changes via XRD; then analyzing superconducting properties using $B_{c2}(T)$ within the WHH framework, noting deviations from conventional limits; finally, confirming the underlying mechanism through normal-state magnetotransport analysis using the Kawabata WL/WAL model.
why_interesting: The direct link established between structural modification (annealing) and the enhancement of a fundamental quantum interaction (spin-orbit coupling) that stabilizes unconventional superconductivity is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
